plate.narration: A dragonling grandmother rings her bell at a prospector on her doorstep. Above the crowded tents, a black tower rises from the ridge. The road has brought everyone this far. Now there are questions to carry uphill.

objectives.label: Read the glassback crab's warning before anybody got pinched
Found the cold cinder wolves something to eat
Listened to the soup-tent woman all the way through

goal.text: Climb to the tower on the ridge, learn what the stones are, and say what it is all for.

steps.label: Learn what the stones really are
Say what it is all for

facet_table.name: The Table Stone
facet_table.text: From the Redspire truth-table. Logged twice. Hums whenever someone tells the truth.

scene_arrival.narration: Climb to the tower on the ridge, learn what the stones are, and say what it is all for. These foothills smell of warm rocks and burnt toast. Above the crowded camps stands a black tower called Redspire Citadel, the Skywardens' watchtower. Below it, a grandmother is ringing a bell at a man digging up her doorstep.

choices.label: Walk up into the foothills
Come down from the broken bridge, in the northeast
Step off the bigfoot high paths, in the west
Walk up through the boundary stones, in the south

scene_door_river.narration: The bridge engineers walk down with you, still arguing about a crack. Behind you lie the bent pride roads and the river toll. Ahead is the tower where their records can meet yours.

choices.label: Down into the camps

scene_door_wild.narration: The MossHome high paths end at a mossy step into ash. A runner waves from the forest side. The moss stops at a ruler-straight line. The runner declines to cross it.

choices.label: Step down into the ash

scene_door_rush.narration: You climb from the boundary stones among the rush wagons. Grandmothers count passing picks with bells. One has switched to a smaller bell to save her arm.

choices.label: Up into the camps

scene_doorstep.narration: Dunmore has planted his claim flag on the grandmother's step. "It hums!" So does every stone here. She rings louder. He goes pink, but holds his pick. Her little round window has curtains.

choices.label: Stand on the doorstep with her, and don't budge
Help him find a humming rock that is nobody's door
Say the one rule, the way grandmothers say it
Have a thornguard plant a shield on the step
Risk stepping in before the grandmother can steady you

check_doorstep.prompt: Stand firm on the grandmother's doorstep so Dunmore cannot dig

onSuccess.narration: You climb onto the step beside the grandmother and plant your feet. Nobody can dig up a doorstep with people standing on it. Dunmore looks at your boots, then at the little round window with curtains in it, and goes pinker than ever. "Sorry," he mumbles, and pulls up his flag. The grandmother gives him a cookie. He is so surprised that he says thank you twice.

onFailure.narration: You climb onto the step, and Dunmore's pick nudges your boots right off it again. Then the grandmother starts ringing her bell right beside his ear. In the end he gives up on the step just to get away from the noise, and stomps off up the slope, rubbing his ear and grumbling about bells.

scene_doorstep_dig_elsewhere.narration: You find Dunmore a humming boulder with no door in it. He proudly plants his flag. The grandmother rings a sweet thank-you. Dunmore waves long after you stop waving back.

choices.label: Walk on up into the foothills

scene_doorstep_one_rule.narration: Your dragonling stands on the step and says it, the way it is said at every dragonling door: "Take what the mountain drops. Never pry at what it holds." Dunmore takes off his hat. "Nobody told me there were rules," he says, very quietly. The grandmother tells him there have always been rules. He writes them on the inside of his hat.

choices.label: Walk on up into the foothills

scene_moths.narration: Embermoths huddle on the cold side of a rock. One refuses to leave a prospector's soup. He has given up and is eating around it. The usual warm cracks lie empty.

choices.label: Follow the moths' line down the slope
Carry the soup moth back to a warm crack
Say it out loud: moths leaving the warm is a warning
Count the moths. All of them.

scene_moths_follow.narration: The moths form an arrow down the slope, all facing away from the mountain. Something glows in the caravan ruts at its point.

choices.label: Go and see what's glowing

scene_moths_coax.narration: You carry the soup moth to a warm crack. It walks straight back out, as if you offered it an oven. The prospector thanks you for returning his soup.

choices.label: Follow the moths down to the road

scene_moths_count.narration: Your bigfoot counts them. All of them. It takes a while, and the prospector with the moth in his soup gets quite impatient. Three hundred and twelve embermoths, and every single one is facing away from the mountain, like an audience that has turned its back on the stage.

choices.label: Follow the moths' line down the slope

scene_moths_say_it.narration: "Moths leaving the warm is a warning," says your dragonling, out loud, in the voice grandmothers use. A grandmother three tents away hears it, stops in the middle of an argument, and rings her hand bell once, sharp, toward the next town. Then she goes back to arguing with a different man on her own doorstep. He has not moved. Neither have the moths.

choices.label: Follow the moths' line down the slope

scene_wolves.narration: Cinder wolves heap themselves in the road like coals with ears. Cold and hungry, they ignore the wagons behind them. Every drover is shouting. None is getting anywhere.

choices.label: Find them something easier to eat than a traffic jam
Fly up and look for what they could eat instead
Wait for them to move on
Have a duskrunner scout the ditches for wolf food

scene_wolves_wait.narration: The wolves eventually stretch and leave together. Every drover claims it was their shouting that worked. The road begins to move.

choices.label: Up the road, toward a smell of soup

scene_wolves_fly_look.narration: From the air you see it at once: a sausage cart tipped on its side in the ditch, a hundred paces down, with the drover long gone. You come down low over the wolves and fly a slow, obvious line toward it. The biggest wolf lifts its nose, understands you perfectly, and the whole pack flows out of the ruts after it like water finding a drain.

choices.label: Up the road, toward a smell of soup

check_wolves.prompt: Find the hungry wolves something better than the road

onSuccess.narration: You spot an overturned sausage cart in the ditch. The wolves spot it two seconds after you. The road clears in a hurry, and one wolf looks back at you as if it is memorizing your face.

onFailure.narration: Your plan involves a sausage on a string, and the wolves are not impressed. In the end they wander off on their own, howling long complaints at the mountain.

scene_claim_boulder.narration: Two prospectors stand on one humming boulder, each with a flag. "Mine." "Mine." Bootlaces tie them to their claims. The watching crowd has brought snacks.

choices.label: Work out whose flag went in first
Tell them to share it, half each
Turn the argument into a show for the crowd
Show them the Unassigned Stone: some stones are nobody's

check_claim.prompt: Find out whose claim flag went into the boulder first

onSuccess.narration: You check the flag holes. Both are brand new. But under the moss at the bottom of the boulder is a third mark, a little carved line, so old the moss has grown into it. It was here before either of them. It was here before anyone. Both prospectors stare at it, untie their bootlaces, and go and find a different boulder, quietly.

onFailure.narration: You measure the flags, count the footprints, and ask the crowd. Everybody gives a different answer, and two people give three. In the end the boulder settles it by humming so loudly that both prospectors hop off at once, and neither of them wants to get back on.

scene_claim_boulder_share.narration: They chalk the round boulder in half, then argue about whose half contains the hum. At least they are sitting now. The crowd applauds the improvement.

choices.label: Up the road to the soup tent

scene_claim_boulder_show.narration: Your kitsune jumps up beside them and turns the argument into a play, with voices. The crowd laughs, then cheers, then votes. The winner gets the boulder. The loser gets everybody's snacks, which turns out to be a much better prize. By the end, the winner is trying to swap.

choices.label: Up the road to the soup tent

scene_claim_boulder_nobodys.narration: You hold up the Unassigned Stone and tell them about the grandmothers' very old list: the caves that are never given to anybody, not ever. The two prospectors look at it for a long time. "Nobody's," says one, trying out the word. "Nobody's," agrees the other. They leave the boulder where it is and go and share a sandwich instead.

choices.label: Up the road to the soup tent

scene_soup_tent.narration: At the top of the road is a soup tent with a sign: FREE, NO QUESTIONS. A woman called Hessa Wren ladles a bowl for {party}, asks for names, and remembers them. Behind her, helpers in painted bark masks stir the pots and hum one low note, all together. "My friends from the Deep Hollow," says Hessa. "The masks are for singing to the mountain." Then she leans in. "The world's laws are broken," she says kindly, as if she were telling you it might rain. "There's a seal on the mountain, like a lid on a pot. It isn't protecting anyone. It's a cage on the cure."

choices.label: Ask her what the cure would fix
Say no thank you, kindly but clearly
Just eat the soup
Notice the mask folded in her apron pocket, and ask about it
Tell her you remember Wend's soup tents on the road north

scene_soup_tent_ford_soup.narration: "Wend's tents, on the north road!" Hessa's face lights up. "Wend sends love. Wend sends love to everybody, but Wend did say your names." She ladles an extra spoonful into each bowl. It is the same soup. It tastes, oddly, like the whole road north.

choices.label: Find somewhere warm to sleep

scene_soup_tent_mask.narration: Your kitsune nods at the painted bark mask folded in her apron pocket. Hessa does not hide it. "For singing in," she says. "The mountain likes a choir." She hums three notes, and the humming stones in your packs hum back before you can stop them. She smiles at that like a gardener at a seedling.

choices.label: Find somewhere warm to sleep

scene_soup_tent_just_soup.narration: You just eat the soup. It is excellent soup, with barley in it and something green. Hessa watches you eat with a look that is mostly kindness and partly patience, and when you hand the bowls back she says, "Tomorrow, then," as if you had an appointment.

choices.label: Find somewhere warm to sleep

scene_soup_tent_no_thanks.narration: "No, thank you," you say, kindly and clearly. Hessa does not argue, and she does not stop smiling, and she does not take the bowl back. "The soup isn't the pitch," she says. "The soup is just soup." You believe her about the soup.

choices.label: Find somewhere warm to sleep

scene_soup_tent_ask_cure.narration: "What would it fix?" Hessa thinks about it properly, which not everyone does. "Who gets to be hungry," she says at last. "Who gets to be cold. Why the sky is the wrong color and nobody with a ledger can say why." She refills your bowl. "Little things," she says. "Everything."

choices.label: Find somewhere warm to sleep

rest_warm_stones.narration: Dragonling neighbors offer warm sleeping-stones. Grandmother Tull rings the ordinary night bell. The unused bell, she says twice, is nothing to worry about. Rest and share your supplies.

choices.label: In the morning, see what the bells are doing

scene_morning_bells.narration: At the morning bench, Grandmother Tull teaches tiny dragonlings the ordinary bell calls. A spare bell sits wrapped in a sock, untouched. "Nothing to worry about." Up the ridge, the citadel watch is listening. Learn the traveling call, ask about the sock, or get supplies before climbing.

choices.label: Sit on the bench and learn the morning ring
Ask about the bell in the sock
Fly the morning ring up the ridge to the next town
Buy a honeycake from the bench stall for 2 coins
Risk ringing the morning call before practicing it

check_bells.prompt: Ring the morning ring in time with the little dragonlings

onSuccess.narration: Ding, ding-ding, ding. You get it right, and the smallest dragonling gives you a solemn nod, as if you had joined something important. Grandmother Tull presses a warm honeycake into your hands for the climb, and tells you the ridge is that way, as if you might have forgotten.

onFailure.narration: Your ring comes out ding, dong, clatter, which in bell code means, as far as anyone can tell, goats, but sideways. The little dragonlings laugh so hard that one falls off the bench. Grandmother Tull says you will get it next time, and points you up the ridge.

scene_morning_bells_sock.narration: Grandmother Tull takes a long breath. "That one has never been rung," she says. "Not by me. Not by my grandmother. Everybody knows what it would mean, and nobody says it." She pats the sock, the way you pat a sleeping dog. "Nothing to worry about." That is four times now, and this time she does not quite look at you.

choices.label: Climb the ridge toward the citadel

scene_morning_bells_fly_ring.narration: You carry a little bell up the ridge and ring it, one, two-two, one, over the next town. Far below, a whole row of tiny bells rings back, very proudly and not quite together. From up here you can see the citadel's black tower, and halfway up the ridge, a crowd gathered around something that glitters.

choices.label: Glide back down and lead the climb

scene_crab.narration: On the ridge, Dunmore raises his pick at a glittering heap. The heap has eyes and claws. A glassback crab rocks from side to side on its warm ground. Another watches from the next burrow. Dunmore really should check for curtains more often.

choices.label: Read what the crab is trying to say
Knock on its burrow stone, and wait
Call to Dunmore by name. He listens to you now.
Pull Dunmore back and face the crab
Back everyone off its warm ground, go the long way

scene_crab_dunmore.narration: "Dunmore!" you call. He knows your voice now, and he stops mid-swing. "Three big steps back." He does it at once, without one word of argument, and the whole crowd steps back with him. The crab lowers its claws, looks Dunmore up and down, and goes back to tidying its pebbles.

choices.label: See what the crab does next

check_crab.prompt: Read the glassback crab's threat display

onSuccess.narration: Two claws up and a rock to the left means: this is my warm ground, and you are standing in my garden. You tell everybody to take three big steps back. The crab lowers its claws and goes back to tidying its pebbles, very pleased.

onFailure.narration: Two claws up and a rock to the left means... you guess "hello." It does not mean hello. The crab charges, and its neighbor from the next burrow scuttles over to see what all the fuss is.

encounter_crab.narration: Two glassback crabs clatter down the switchbacks, their shells flashing every color of the gems around them.

onVictory.narration: Both crabs back off onto their own warm ground, and the moment they get there, they forget you ever existed. It took all morning, though. The sun is high by the time you reach the citadel road.

onDefeat.narration: The crabs nudge you, very firmly, all the way down the ridge and off their warm ground, then go back to their gardening. You are fine. You are also at the bottom of the ridge again, and the afternoon is nearly gone.

check_late_gate.prompt: Race the sunset up the ridge before the citadel gate closes

onSuccess.narration: You run the switchbacks two at a time and slide in under the gate as it comes down, with one finger's width to spare.

onFailure.narration: The gate comes down with a BOOM just as you get there. A warden on the wall gives you a sad little shrug. Rules are rules, even for heroes.

scene_crab_thanks.narration: Dunmore lowers his pick. The crab rearranges three pebbles like a thank-you note. Go straight to the citadel for an early arrival, or help the crowd settle first and spend the morning here.

choices.label: Straight up the ridge road, right now
Fly ahead and tell the gate you're coming
Help Dunmore and the crowd find a better spot first

scene_crab_thanks_help_dunmore.narration: You spend the morning finding the crowd a patch without a crab underneath. By the last tent, the sun is high. The citadel road waits in shadow.

choices.label: Up the ridge road at last

scene_crab_thanks_fly_ahead.narration: You fly ahead up the ridge and land on the citadel wall, which is apparently not allowed. The warden on the gate looks up, looks at the ledger in his hand, and sighs. By the time the climb is done, the gate is already open and a clerk is already waiting with two ledgers.

choices.label: Go in

scene_citadel_gate.narration: Redspire's windows all face up. Inside, clerk Pellam logs your names twice. "The captain has a table." He checks both entries, then remembers the notebook for people he has met twice.

choices.label: Pellam! From the bridge! How are you here first?
Follow Pellam to the table
Ask why every window faces up

scene_citadel_gate_windows.narration: "So we see it first," says Pellam, as if it were obvious. "Whatever the mountain does, a warden is watching, and a warden is writing it down." He points at a narrow stair that winds up and up. "Four hundred years of watching. Most nights the log says nothing." He looks proud. "Nothing is the best thing a log can say."

choices.label: Follow Pellam down the hall

scene_citadel_gate_desk.narration: ANYTHING THAT HUMS, LOG IT HERE. Pellam dips his pen by the desk. He waits politely, like a cat at a mouse hole. He can log the packs, explain the records, or recognize an existing tag.

choices.label: Tip out your packs and let him log everything
Ask what the log is for, first
Show him the Clerk's Stone, already tagged at the bridge

scene_citadel_gate_desk_tip_out.narration: Pellam logs what you show him, draws tiny pictures, then hands it back. He stamps your hands LOGGED. "Honest on paper. The best kind." The ink will last for days.

choices.label: On to the captain's table

scene_citadel_gate_desk_ask_why.narration: Pellam turns the big log around so you can see. Page after page of stones, four hundred years of them: every gem that ever rolled down the mountain, written down, then written down again. "Every one of them went somewhere," he says. "Nobody ever wrote down where." He taps the newest page. It is full. So is the one before it.

choices.label: On to the captain's table

scene_citadel_gate_desk_clerks.narration: Pellam looks at the little tag on the Clerk's Stone, then at the handwriting on it, which is his own. "Logged at the bridge," he breathes. "Carried up. Here." He has to sit down. It is the happiest anyone has ever seen a clerk. He waves you on without opening a single pack, and writes the word HOME next to the stone.

choices.label: On to the captain's table

scene_pellam_again.narration: Pellam does not look up from the second ledger. "The bridge is logged," he says. "The citadel needed logging. I go where the ledgers are." He writes your names a third time, in a very small notebook he keeps for people he has met twice. "Irregular," he says. "Entirely legal. This way. The captain has a table."

choices.label: Follow Pellam down the hall

scene_truth_table.narration: Captain Orla Voss waits at a long table of watch-logs and one humming stone. She commands the Skywardens. "Show us what the road taught you." Compare the dated records yourselves, or ask the wardens to read and answer questions.

choices.label: Let the wardens read their logs out first
Work it out yourselves before anybody reads a log
Show the troll's question, sash-maps and bridge survey
Show the wounded glades, the path archive and the knot-cord
Show the relay's spiral verses and the boundary tallies
Set Mother Thrum's tuned charm on the table
Point at the one ledger bound in a different color
Risk fitting the clues together without comparing dates

scene_truth_table_puzzle.prompt: Put the foothills together before the wardens read their logs

onSuccess.narration: You lay the last two days on the table: moths facing away, wolves too cold to hunt, a crab guarding its warm ground, a whole hillside of stones humming one note. "Everything up here is leaning away from the mountain," you say. Captain Voss pushes the oldest log across the table. "So did we," she says. "Four hundred years ago."

onFailure.narration: You lay out the moths, the wolves and the crab, and they go around and around and will not join up. Pellam clears his throat, very kindly, and opens the oldest log. "It took us four hundred years," he says. "You have had two days."

scene_truth_table_odd_ledger.narration: Your bigfoot points at the one ledger bound in a different color, half under the others. Pellam looks as if he has been caught stealing cookies. "That one's not read," he says. "It's only kept." Captain Voss holds out her hand, and Pellam gives it to her, and the room gets a lot quieter.

choices.label: Watch it all click together

scene_truth_table_rush_clues.narration: The boundary tallies, relay verse account and old watch-log bend around the same places. Voss slides them side by side. Pellam checks their dates, twice.

choices.label: Watch it all click together

scene_truth_table_wild_clues.narration: You describe the wounded glades and MossHome archive. Pellam compares the forest's record with the old watch-log. "The forest keeps records too," says Voss. Put their dates together.

choices.label: Watch it all click together

scene_truth_table_river_clues.narration: Pellam sets a four-hundred-year-old log beside the bridge survey and sash-map account. Its faded question matches the troll's: WHERE DID YOU GET THAT, AND WHERE IS IT GOING? Compare their dates.

choices.label: Watch it all click together

scene_whole_truth.narration: Your clues and the wardens' logs click together like a puzzle. The gemstones are pieces of a seal. The seal holds a titan asleep under Mount Red Sky. And the rush is taking the seal apart, one pocket at a time. In the middle of it all, the gemstone on the table hums. The wardens have given it a name and a number, and Pellam has logged it twice. One very old line just says: an old stone gate, far away in a western marsh, hums the same note. Next to it, in three different handwritings: nobody knows why.

choices.label: Ask to carry the stone (Pellam logs it a third time)
Leave the stone where it is, in warden custody

scene_whole_truth_leave_stone.narration: "Custody," says Voss. Pellam adds it to both entries. Three records, no travel. The stone keeps humming on the table.

choices.label: Hear the captain's plan

scene_whole_truth_take_stone.narration: Pellam logs the Table Stone under WITH THEM and slides it across. It hums against your palm while Voss unrolls her map. Everyone watches; nobody objects.

choices.label: Hear the captain's plan

scene_acceptable_losses.narration: Voss circles three towns on her map. "Acceptable losses." Her voice is calm. The words are not. A humming note fills the silence after them.

choices.label: Tell her a town is not a number
Hear the whole plan before you say anything
Roar, very politely, at the map

scene_acceptable_losses_polite_roar.narration: Your manticore roars at the map. It is a polite roar, with a please in it, and it still makes the parchment curl up at the corners and every pen in the room roll off its table. Captain Voss waits until the last pen has stopped. Then she flattens the map, picks up a pencil, and redraws one circle so it misses a town.

choices.label: Step over to the window

scene_acceptable_losses_hear_plan.narration: Close the roads from the Pinch, the narrow gap ahead. Empty three towns. Stop stones going either way. Voss explains each step. It is careful and honest. You can hear the humming when she finishes.

choices.label: Step over to the window

scene_acceptable_losses_not_a_number.narration: "A town is not a number," you say. Captain Voss looks at the map for a long moment. "No," she says. "It's three numbers. Houses, people, bells." Then, much quieter, so only your table hears: "I know." She does not rub the circles out. She does draw one of them a little smaller.

choices.label: Step over to the window

scene_whole_truth_window.narration: Pellam allows one cup of tea before the record. Three lights shine below: Hessa's moving lantern, the glittering camps, and the gathering towns' bells. Which do you watch?

choices.label: Hessa's lantern, moving through the camp
The glittering camps, full of stones
The bell towers of the dragonling towns
Look for the wolf that knows you
Look up, the way the windows do
Ring Grandmother Tull's morning ring, very softly

scene_whole_truth_window_soup.narration: Hessa's lantern is the only light that moves. She is carrying soup out to the edge of the camp, to the tents nobody else visits. Wherever she stops, somebody sits up. It looks very kind from up here. It looks very certain, too. Pellam, beside you, writes nothing at all, and keeps watching.

choices.label: Back to the table for the record

scene_whole_truth_window_camps.narration: The camps glitter like a dropped necklace. Every tent has a stone in it, and every stone catches a little firelight. It is the most beautiful thing in the foothills. When you hold very still you can hear it, too: thousands of stones, all humming the same old note, very softly, a long way from home.

choices.label: Back to the table for the record

scene_whole_truth_window_bells.narration: One by one, the dragonling towns ring their night bell, the ordinary one, passed up the dark from town to town like a lantern handed along a line. When the last town rings, they all go quiet together. Captain Voss counts every ring under her breath, and looks a little more relieved at each one.

choices.label: Back to the table for the record

scene_whole_truth_window_wolf.narration: Down on the dark road, one small glow sits apart from its pack, round with sausage, looking up at the citadel. It is the wolf from the road. Cinder wolves do not wave. This one thumps its tail on the ground twice, which is close, and then curls up facing your window.

choices.label: Back to the table for the record

scene_whole_truth_window_look_up.narration: You look up instead, the way the whole citadel does. Over Mount Red Sky the sky is a deep, wrong red, and right at the top the mountain lets out a slow puff of ash, like somebody breathing in their sleep. "Every night for four hundred years," says Pellam softly, "somebody has stood here and written that down. Tonight it's me."

choices.label: Back to the table for the record

scene_whole_truth_window_ring.narration: Ding, ding-ding, ding, very softly, out of the window into the dark. For a moment nothing happens. Then, far below, a very small bell answers: ding, dong, clatter. The smallest dragonling is still up, practicing. Captain Voss turns away from the window so that nobody can see whether she is smiling.

choices.label: Back to the table for the record

scene_ledger.narration: Pellam opens a fresh page. "What have you been doing, all this way?" Tell the account in your own words, or point to something your party did. He leaves room for the whole answer.

choices.label: Tell it plainly, in your own words
Show the harvest sprites' woven medal
Tell how the wounded glade closed up
Say why you really came: somebody had to
Admit the sprites are still talking about you
Set the Glade Stone on the table
Tip out your pockets, Ember Facet first
Say why you really came: to get rich
Ask what the power under the mountain could actually do
Ask who gets to hold that power
Repeat what Hessa said about the cure

variants.text: The page beside your names stays short. Pellam writes down a hum, and not much else.
Beside your names Pellam lists the great stones you carry: {facets} so far, each one logged twice.
Pellam has to turn to a second page for the great stones you carry: {facets}, and every one of them logged twice.
Pellam records your first reason from the city: treasure. He has heard that answer before.
Your first reason was finding out what happened. "Today you did," says Pellam.
You wanted your names known. Pellam writes them extra big.
You came to keep people safe. Pellam nods before writing it.
You came for a fresh start. Pellam finds a clean page.
You came to prove you could. "Here you are," says Pellam.
Under WHICH ROAD he writes: the river roads, past the prides and over the broken bridge.
Under WHICH ROAD he writes: the forest roads, through MossHome and along the bigfoot high paths.
Under WHICH ROAD he writes: the rush roads, up the caravan road and past the boundary stones.

scene_reading_restore.narration: Pellam reads it all back and taps the page. "Helping. Fixing. Putting things back where they belong," he says. "That adds up to one word, and the word is return." Captain Voss raises one eyebrow, which for her is practically a parade.

choices.label: Hear the next question

scene_reading_hoard.narration: Pellam reads it back, and the stones in your packs hum along with every line. "Pockets," he says. "A great many pockets. That adds up to a collection." Nobody in the room says he is wrong. A moth lands on your bag, thinks about it, and leaves.

choices.label: Hear the next question

scene_reading_leash.narration: Pellam reads it back slowly. "Questions about what the power could do. Who holds it. What it's for." He writes one word and underlines it twice: leash. Somewhere below, Hessa's soup tent is still serving.

choices.label: Hear the next question

scene_who_to_tell.narration: Who should stand with you now: the wardens, the gathering grandmothers, or nobody else yet? You can keep the promise you made on the road, or choose a different audience after what you learned. Voss waits.

choices.label: Stand with the wardens' plan
Take it to the grandmothers and the gathering-law towns
Keep it close and tell nobody else
Keep the promise you already made to the wardens
Keep faith with the gatherers you already told
Keep the secret you were already keeping

scene_kept_close_room.narration: "Nobody else," says Captain Voss. The room is quiet. "Then you had better be right," she says, "and you had better be quick." Pellam writes nothing at all, which he tells you later is the best entry a ledger can have.

choices.label: Hear the real question

scene_told_gatherers_room.narration: "Grandmothers," says Captain Voss, and sighs the sigh of somebody who has argued with grandmothers before. "Very well. They are at least thorough." Pellam writes BELLS in the ledger and underlines it, and somewhere far below, right on cue, one rings.

choices.label: Hear the real question

scene_told_wardens_room.narration: Captain Voss nods once, which is as much as she ever nods. "Then you'll want to know the plan properly," she says, and Pellam opens a fresh ledger with WARDENS AND PARTY on the spine, which he has clearly had ready for some time.

choices.label: Hear the real question

scene_what_for.narration: "And you? What is it all for?" asks Voss. Choose your next road: return the stones, finish the collection, or learn to hold the power. At the mountain you will face the question again. You can also say nothing and leave on the return road for now.

choices.label: Put it back. Every stone.
Finish the collection
Take the leash on what's under the mountain
Say nothing: leave on the return road

scene_declared_leash.narration: "Hold it. The leash." Voss and Pellam look at one another. "Our plan, in fewer words," she says. Below the window, the soup-tent choir hums.

choices.label: Hear Pellam read back the record

scene_record_leash.narration: "Leash," Pellam says, and writes it down and underlines it twice. "Holding is harder than asking. You have to know you are choosing it." Captain Voss closes the book.

variants.text: Pellam reads the first entry: the city's warm stone, sold the same day.
Pellam reads the first entry: the city's warm stone, kept.
Then the harvest field, and the sprites who are still your friends. He draws a tiny star beside it.
Then the harvest field, and the stone you took from the sprites. He reads that one twice, without a word.
Then the wounded glade, green again because of you.
Then the wounded glade, and the stone you took out of its heart.
"Helping. Fixing. Putting things back," he reads. "None of that is the same as holding the leash."
"Pockets. A great many pockets," he reads. "None of that is the same as holding the leash."
"Questions about the power, and who gets to hold it," he reads. "You have been asking about the leash the whole way up."

choices.label: Go and find your bunks

scene_declared_hoard.narration: "Finish the collection." Voss considers it. "Then I will write you down as weather." Pellam writes WEATHER, then adds a question mark. The ink takes a long time to dry.

choices.label: Hear Pellam read back the record

scene_record_hoard.narration: "Collection," Pellam says, and writes COLLECT in his neatest hand, with a small question mark beside it. Captain Voss watches the ink dry. "You will have to live up to that word," she says.

variants.text: Pellam reads the first entry: the city's warm stone, sold the same day.
Pellam reads the first entry: the city's warm stone, kept.
Then the harvest field, and the sprites who are still your friends. He draws a tiny star beside it.
Then the harvest field, and the stone you took from the sprites. He reads that one twice, without a word.
Then the wounded glade, green again because of you.
Then the wounded glade, and the stone you took out of its heart.
"Helping. Fixing. Putting things back," he reads. "That is a different word from the one you just said."
"Pockets. A great many pockets," he reads. "Nobody can say you didn't warn us."
"Questions about the power, and who gets to hold it," he reads. "That is a different word from the one you just said."

choices.label: Go and find your bunks

scene_declared_restore.narration: "Put it back. Every stone." The table answers with one clear note. Voss unfolds her arms. "Then we need the stones coming north tomorrow. Rest first."

choices.label: Hear Pellam read back the record

scene_record_restore.narration: "Put it back," Pellam says, and writes RETURN beside your names in his neatest hand. He leaves a little space after it, in case the road teaches you something else. Captain Voss watches him write, then nods.

variants.text: Pellam reads the first entry: the city's warm stone, sold the same day.
Pellam reads the first entry: the city's warm stone, kept.
Then the harvest field, and the sprites who are still your friends. He draws a tiny star beside it.
Then the harvest field, and the stone you took from the sprites. He reads that one twice, without a word.
Then the wounded glade, green again because of you.
Then the wounded glade, and the stone you took out of its heart.
"Helping. Fixing. Putting things back," he reads. "The pages and the promise say the same thing."
"Pockets. A great many pockets," he reads. "And now you say put it back. That is a long way to turn around. People do."
"Questions about the power, and who gets to hold it," he reads. "And now you say put it back. People do turn around."

choices.label: Go and find your bunks

scene_undeclared.narration: Pellam writes RETURN? with a question mark. "A starting road, then," says Voss. "You can carry a question as well as a plan." She leaves your earlier promises in the record. Nobody invents an answer for each hero.

choices.label: Go and find your bunks

rest_end_ashfall.narration: The wardens give you bunks in a room where every window faces up. Far below, the mountain turns over in its sleep, and every embermoth in the foothills shuffles one step farther away from it. You know what the stones are now, and you know what you want. Rest. Tomorrow, everything you passed on the road comes back up the mountain to meet you.

variants.text: The traveling call you learned brought a lantern to the gate.
Your record includes the people who helped compare the evidence.

scene_shut_out.narration: You spend the night outside the gate with the rush's leftovers, while down below the dragonling towns go to bed with their bells on. At midnight a little hatch opens, and a warden clerk called Pellam passes the wardens' old watch-logs out by lantern, one page at a time, and reads you the oldest line. The gemstones are pieces of a seal. The seal holds a titan asleep under Mount Red Sky. And the rush is taking it apart, one pocket at a time. "What is it all for?" he whispers. Take time to hear one another before answering.

choices.label: Put it back. Every stone.
Finish the collection
Take the leash on what's under the mountain
Say nothing: leave on the return road

scene_shut_out_refuse.narration: "The return road for now," Pellam whispers after your silence. "The question stays open." He passes a blanket through the hatch, then another.

choices.label: Sleep against the wall

scene_shut_out_leash.narration: "Hold it," you whisper. "The leash." The pen stops. "That's my captain's word," Pellam whispers, sounding puzzled, and passes out a blanket and a very small book with CAGE on the spine, which he asks you to give back in the morning.

choices.label: Sleep against the wall

scene_shut_out_hoard.narration: "Finish the collection," you whisper. There is a pause behind the hatch. "Noted," Pellam whispers at last, and then, after another pause, a blanket comes through anyway.

choices.label: Sleep against the wall

scene_shut_out_restore.narration: "Put it back," you whisper through the hatch. Pellam's pen scratches. "Good," he whispers back, which is not a thing clerks say, and passes out a blanket after the lantern.

choices.label: Sleep against the wall

rest_end_shut_out.narration: You sleep against the cold side of the citadel wall, like the embermoths. The crabs, the sunset and the gate all beat you today, and the mountain noticed: the tremors have settled into a slow, patient rhythm. But the whole truth is in your heads now, and Pellam has left his lantern hanging on the wall for you. It burns all night.

variants.text: The traveling call you learned brought a lantern to the gate.
Your record includes the people who helped compare the evidence.

scene_crab_long_way.narration: You back everybody off the warm ground, Dunmore last and grumbling, and take the goat track around the ridge instead. The crab goes back to its pebbles. The goat track is a goat's idea of a road, and by the time it brings you out on the citadel side, the sun is high and the whole morning is gone.

choices.label: Up the ridge road at last

scene_truth_table_charm.narration: You set Mother Thrum's tuned charm on the table. The moment it touches the stone it rings, and the stone on the table rings back, and every warden in the room stops writing at once. Captain Voss waits for the note to die. It takes a long time.

choices.label: Watch it all click together

interaction_moth_trail.narration: One moth glows brighter, then hides between three flat rocks. Follow where it ends up. The soup prospector watches too. He has moved his bowl well out of range.

interaction.cue: Watch the glowing moth hide, then pick the rock it ends up under.

onSuccess.narration: You pick the right rock. The moth pops out glowing like a tiny stove, gives the prospector a smug look, and flutters off down the slope toward the caravan road, as if it had somewhere to be.

onFailure.narration: You pick the wrong rock. The moth peeks out from the right one and, if a moth can giggle, giggles. Then it zips off down the slope toward the caravan road, and you follow.

interaction_wagons.narration: A wagon wheel is stuck in a rut, blocking the road again. Hold it steady while the acting hero steers. The centaur drover will pull. Everybody behind you offers excellent advice.

interaction.cue: Friends push the wagon while someone steers.

onSuccess.narration: The wheel pops out of the rut with a sound like a cork. Forty wagons cheer, forty drovers claim it was their idea, and the centaur drover presses three coins into your hand. "Toll refund," the drover says. "Do not ask which toll."

onFailure.narration: The wagon rolls back, then forward, then sideways. In the end the faun drover hitches a goat to it, and it pops out of the rut all by itself. Everybody pretends that was the plan.

onAssisted.narration: The drovers lean in beside you, and together you rock the wagon free. It pops out of the rut with a sound like a cork, and the centaur drover presses three coins into your hand. "Toll refund," the drover says. "Do not ask which toll."

interaction_soup_pots.narration: You join Hessa's helpers with the supper pots. They fill the gaps in the line and carry the hot handles beside you. At the last tent, a tired prospector cups a bowl and stops shivering. Hessa wraps a supper for your pack. "For the road," she says.

choices.label: Continue together

scene_morning_bells_bought.narration: The stall by the bench belongs to a dragonling baker with flour on both ears. Two coins buys a honeycake as big as a fist, still warm. "Eat on the way up," says the baker. "The ridge is steep, and the citadel is not going anywhere." You tuck the honeycake into your pack.

choices.label: Climb the ridge toward the citadel

scene_crawlers_hall.narration: Bone crawlers clack up the cellar stairs toward the humming packs. Bread-sized beetles, fond of table legs. Pellam points toward the old logs. "Please get them downstairs before they find those." His pen is still moving.

choices.label: Herd the crawlers back to the cellar

encounter_crawlers.narration: The bone crawlers clack along the gallery, chasing the hum in your packs. Herd them back to the cellar stairs before they reach the old logs.

scene_crawlers_home.narration: The last crawler clacks down the cellar stairs, and Pellam shuts the door and writes CRAWLERS: HOME. Then he presses a tin whistle into your hand, stamped with a tiny tower. "Warden's issue," he says. "For loud moments. Log it if you use it." He straightens his collar. "Now. Before the captain, the tags."

choices.label: Let Pellam tag your stones

scene_crawlers_rescued.narration: A line of wardens marches in with brooms and sweeps the crawlers down the stairs like autumn leaves. Nobody is hurt. A warden hands out hot tea and a blanket, and the old logs are safe. You do not get a whistle for this one, but Pellam writes your names in the margin anyway. Then he straightens his collar. "Now. Before the captain, the tags."

choices.label: Let Pellam tag your stones

interaction_tags.narration: Every humming thing in the citadel gets a tag, and Pellam holds up the tag pictures one at a time. "Watch them go by," he says, "then put them back in the same order. The captain likes things in order."

interaction.cue: Watch the tags light up, then tap them back in order.

onSuccess.narration: Moon, flame, leaf, flame. Pellam gives a tiny, rare smile and stamps each tag. "In the right order," he says. "The captain will be thrilled. She will not show it."

onFailure.narration: You swap two of the tags. Pellam sighs, fixes them with his pen, and writes a very small note in the margin. "Order matters," he says kindly. "It will do. The captain is waiting."

interaction_tea.narration: Pellam pours the promised tea while you make space at the table. Captain Voss takes the smallest cup and drinks without a word. For a little while, the only question is whether anyone wants more. Then Pellam turns to a fresh page.

choices.label: Continue together

interaction_doorstep.narration: Stand with the grandmother while the acting hero guides Dunmore's pick away from her step. Keep the space steady; alone, use the doorpost. Her cookie tin is firmly behind the door. The pick is getting no closer to it.

interaction.cue: Hold the doorstep clear while the pick is guided aside.

onSuccess.narration: You climb onto the step beside the grandmother and plant your feet. Nobody can dig up a doorstep with people standing on it. Dunmore looks at your boots, then at the little round window with curtains in it, and goes pinker than ever. "Sorry," he mumbles, and pulls up his flag. The grandmother gives him a cookie. He is so surprised that he says thank you twice.

onFailure.narration: You climb onto the step, and Dunmore's pick nudges your boots right off it again. Then the grandmother starts ringing her bell right beside his ear. In the end he gives up on the step just to get away from the noise, and stomps off up the slope, rubbing his ear and grumbling about bells.

onAssisted.narration: The grandmother braces the doorframe beside you. Together you hold the step clear. Dunmore apologizes and remembers your voices.

interaction_morning_ring.narration: Grandmother Tull teaches a traveling call: one ring, two quick rings, one ring. Watch, then echo it. The ridge watch knows this call too, useful if you need someone to notice you at the gate. The smallest dragonling conducts with a spoon.

interaction.cue: Watch the traveling call, then ring it in the same order.

onSuccess.narration: Ding, ding-ding, ding. You get it right, and the smallest dragonling gives you a solemn nod, as if you had joined something important. Grandmother Tull presses a warm honeycake into your hands for the climb, and tells you the ridge is that way, as if you might have forgotten.

onFailure.narration: Your ring comes out ding, dong, clatter, which in bell code means, as far as anyone can tell, goats, but sideways. The little dragonlings laugh so hard that one falls off the bench. Grandmother Tull says you will get it next time, and points you up the ridge.

onAssisted.narration: Tull rings beside you while you echo the call. With her help, you learn it and earn a honeycake for the climb.

scene_gate_recovery.narration: Back at the bottom of the ridge, the gate is starting to close. Run the switchbacks, or call the ridge watch with the traveling pattern if you learned it. Decide how to ask for help. A goat waits at the shortest bend.

choices.label: Run the switchbacks before the gate closes
Call the ridge watch with the pattern you learned

interaction_gate_call.narration: Call the watch with the pattern from the morning: one, two quick, one. You tap the rhythm on the gate bell. A warden on the wall lifts a lantern to listen. There is time to share the pattern before ringing.

interaction.cue: Echo the traveling call for the ridge watch.

onSuccess.narration: The watch answers the call and holds the gate while you climb. You arrive late in the day, with help.

onFailure.narration: The watch cannot make out the call before the gate shuts. A lantern stays lit by the hatch for you.

onAssisted.narration: The watch echoes the first ring. You finish together, and the warden holds the gate for your climb.

interaction_truth_timeline.narration: Pellam lays out three dated records: an old watch-log, the eruption report, and this season's road accounts. Share the dates and put the records in time order. Compare what changed and what was already happening. One page has a four-hundred-year-old tea ring.

interaction.cue: Share the dated evidence and place oldest to newest.
clues: The watch-log records the same humming note before the great eruption.
The great eruption happened before the road accounts you brought.
This season's road accounts are the newest records.

onSuccess.narration: You compare the old note with the eruption and the road changes. Voss opens the oldest explanation beside your checked dates.

onFailure.narration: Pellam reads the dates beside you and corrects their order. Voss brings the oldest explanation to the table.

onAssisted.narration: Pellam checks each date with you. Together you compare the records before Voss opens the oldest explanation.

interaction_watch_logs.narration: Let the wardens read the logs, and stop them to ask questions. Each hero chooses something to check or offers a road observation. Pellam finds the oldest page under a newer page labeled READ THIS FIRST. He is offended on behalf of both pages.

choices.label: Ask how old the matching note is
Describe a change on our road
Ask what the records cannot explain

interaction_purpose_council.narration: Before choosing a road, hear every hero. Say what you hope to protect, what you still need to know, or what you are willing to try. You may ask for help finding words. Pellam puts his pen down. For once, the ledger can wait.

choices.label: Say what I want to protect
Ask what our plan might cost
Say what I am willing to try

interaction_watch_logs_response_date.narration: Pellam points to the old date and reads it aloud. The wardens answer your questions and compare the dated records. Voss turns to their oldest explanation.

choices.label: Continue together

interaction_watch_logs_response_road.narration: Voss sets your observation beside the watch records. The wardens answer your questions and compare the dated records. Voss turns to their oldest explanation.

choices.label: Continue together

interaction_watch_logs_response_question.narration: Pellam separates the recorded facts from the questions still open. The wardens answer your questions and compare the dated records. Voss turns to their oldest explanation.

choices.label: Continue together

interaction_purpose_council_response_pro.narration: The table listens to what you hope to keep safe. Everyone has had a turn. Now choose the party's next road together.

choices.label: Continue together

interaction_purpose_council_response_ask.narration: Voss hears your question and leaves time for everyone to discuss it. Everyone has had a turn. Now choose the party's next road together.

choices.label: Continue together

interaction_purpose_council_response_try.narration: Pellam listens without putting a choice beside your name. Everyone has had a turn. Now choose the party's next road together.

choices.label: Continue together

interaction_soup_pots.narration: Pass Hessa's heavy soup pot along to the tents with no supper. "Many hands. No hurry." Every helper takes a handle. One prospector measures his bowl against the pot, hopefully.

interaction.cue: Catch the pot, then pass it on.

onSuccess.narration: The pot goes from hand to hand to hand, all the way to the edge of the camp, and not a drop is lost. A tired prospector takes a bowl in both hands and closes his eyes. Hessa wraps a supper in a cloth and tucks it into your pack. "For the road," she says. It is a very nice supper.

onFailure.narration: The pot wobbles, and half the soup goes into a prospector's boots. He says it is the warmest his feet have been all week. Hessa laughs, and the pots go on.

onAssisted.narration: Hessa's helpers fill the gaps in the line, and the pot goes from hand to hand to the edge of the camp without a drop lost. Hessa wraps a supper in a cloth and tucks it into your pack. "For the road," she says.

interaction_tea.narration: Back at the table, Pellam keeps his word about the tea. The kettle is the size of a bucket, and the cups are the size of thimbles. "Everybody helps with tea," he says. "It is in the regulations. Page nine."

interaction.cue: Make the tea: pour it, stir it and share the shortbread.

options.label: Pour the tea
options.reaction: A thin gold stream fills a thimble cup without a drop spilled.

options.label: Stir it slowly
options.reaction: The tea swirls round and round, and a warden leans in to watch.

options.label: Pass the shortbread
options.reaction: Pellam takes one piece and logs it. Then he takes another piece and does not log it.

stages: Everybody has a cup and a piece of shortbread.

onSuccess.narration: The tea is only slightly too hot. Captain Voss drinks hers in one go without a word, and puts the cup down very gently, which from her is a compliment. Pellam turns to a fresh page.

onFailure.narration: The tea is only slightly too hot. Captain Voss drinks hers in one go without a word, and puts the cup down very gently, which from her is a compliment. Pellam turns to a fresh page.
